title: Delete installRequirementsCommand — the last of the dead per-node pip data
description: Raised from MPI-630, which deleted `pipPins` for exactly this reason and left the twin behind. `installRequirementsCommand` is the same dead data one field over: since MPI-413 neither engine resolves a pack's requirements.txt, so nothing executes it. Local — routes/downloadManager.js says "No per-node requirements step here any more"; remote — routes/remoteModels.js:438 sends no `install_command` passthrough and the Pod wrapper accepts+IGNORES it (wrapper.py:2498, README:155 "The wrapper runs no pip at all"); the Pod Dockerfile's MPI-413 comment says the curated set "also retires the per-pack installRequirementsCommand" outright. It survives on two entries in js/data/modelConstants/nodesDeps.js: 'python install.py' (ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation) and the controlnet_aux non-upgrade pip line. The live risk is the test, not the field: tests/controlnet-aux-torch-guard.test.cjs points 1-3 still assert the command exists, starts with bare `python`, and carries no --upgrade — an assertion about a code path that no longer runs, which is precisely the shape that made ComfyUI-MelodramaBox invent pipPins to go green (see memory/feedback_a_guard_test_keeps_dead_data_alive.md). Remove both fields, delete assertions 1-3 (keep 5/6: the baked-vs-code-only installRequirements split is still live and load-bearing), and re-check `node scripts/compile-node-deps.mjs --check` — Frame-Interpolation resolves requirements-no-cupy.txt through that path, so confirm python_deps.in still covers it before deleting the command that named it. PRE-CHECK, same gate MPI-630 used: if any pip run of a pack's requirements survives anywhere, close this as rejected instead.
